t: 3276. Select Cells in Grid With Maximum Score
o: Pick cells with pairwise distinct rows and pairwise distinct values to maximize the sum. The grid is at most 10 x 10 with values in 1..100, so at most 10 cells are picked and at most 100 distinct values exist. The row constraint is tiny (bitmask over 10 rows), which suggests a DP over values with a row-occupancy mask. Example 1 picks 1, 3, 4 for a score of 8; example 2 picks 7 and 8 (two 8s cannot both be used) for 15.
k: Only the row-occupancy bitmask (<= 2^10 states) needs to be tracked; the value-uniqueness constraint is handled by processing each distinct value once.
dp[mask] = best score using processed values with occupied rows = mask; for each value, skip it or place it in any free row containing it.
Processing distinct values in any fixed order guarantees each value is used at most once.

a.n: Approach 1: DP over Distinct Values with Row Bitmask
a.i: Enumerate distinct values one at a time. For each value v and each current mask, we may leave v unused (carry dp[mask]) or place it in a row r that contains v and is free, transitioning to mask | 1<<r with score + v. Because each value is considered exactly once, uniqueness holds automatically; the mask enforces distinct rows. With D <= 100 distinct values, 1024 masks, and 10 rows this is roughly 1e6 transitions.
s: Collect has[v] = set of rows containing value v.
For each distinct v: new_dp = dp; for each mask and free row r in has[v], relax new_dp[mask | 1<<r] with dp[mask] + v.
Return the maximum dp over all masks (nonempty selections dominate since values are positive).
a.t: O(D · 2^m · m) ≈ 1e6 for D <= 100 distinct values and m <= 10 rows
a.sp: O(2^m) for the DP arrays plus O(cell count) for the value->rows map

a.i: Process rows top to bottom; at each row either skip it or pick one of its values not yet used (deduplicating repeated values within the row to avoid redundant branches). This directly mirrors the problem statement and is fast enough at 10 x 10 thanks to pruning, though asymptotically worse than the bitmask DP.
s: Recurse on row index r with a used-values set and accumulated score.
Branch 2: for each distinct unused value in row r, mark it used, recurse, unmark.
At r == m, update the global best.
a.t: Exponential in theory, but pruning (per-row value dedup, used-set) keeps it practical for 10 x 10
a.sp: O(m + distinct values) for recursion and the used set

w: The bitmask DP is the interview-ready answer: polynomial, and it cleanly separates the two constraints (values via processing order, rows via the mask). Note the Java sketch above simplifies value lookup — in production code carry the value alongside its row list. At least one cell must be selected; since all values are positive, max over dp is always a nonempty selection. Follow-up: LC 3259 asks for k up to 5000 rooks — there the value-domain DP with 'best two values per row' tricks is required.
